summary:
RULING-PHASE RECOMMENDATION: WHERE THE NON-FINITE REFUSAL BELONGS.
Read all six reports at .rework/audits/sweep_*.json (828 cells over the 207 numeric levers). Then
ran 40 further configurations of my own, because the six sweeps drove four values and the ruling
turns on a value none of them drove. NOTHING IN THE REPOSITORY WAS EDITED; every measurement below
is from /tmp/rule/ or from a patched COPY of the tree at /tmp/rule/tree.

=====================================================================================
RECOMMENDATION, IN ORDER OF WHAT I WOULD LAND
=====================================================================================

R0. LAND THE OverflowError TOKEN FIRST, AND DO NOT MAKE IT WAIT ON THE ARCHITECTURAL RULING.
    src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce catches `(TypeError, ValueError)`. Adding OverflowError to that
    tuple converts every int lever at +/-inf from a bare traceback to the tree's own refusal idiom.
    MEASURED (patched copy, /tmp/rule/t1p.py): ZZ_N='inf' -> "LeverError: ZZ_N='inf' is not a int",
    against "OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer" on the real tree
    (/tmp/rule/t1.py). It is 110 int levers x 2 values = 220 cells tree-wide; every one of the six
    reports names it as its largest REFUSED_BADLY block. It carries NO policy content: nan already
    takes the ValueError branch on the same line and produces the correct message, so this makes
    inf agree with nan rather than deciding anything new. Land it alone.

R1. ADOPT (a) AS THE FLOOR: one finiteness refusal in src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce, with a
    per-Lever opt-out, behind ONE module constant `REFUSE_NON_FINITE = True`.

R2. ADOPT (b) AS THE ANSWER, INCREMENTALLY AND NOT AS A BIG BANG: add `domain=(lo, hi)` to the
    Lever declaration, in the shape `choices=` already has, and populate it lever by lever starting
    with the twenty on the work list below. A lever with no `domain=` keeps exactly today's
    behaviour plus R1's floor, so this is not a 207-declaration migration before anything ships.

R3. REJECT (c) and (d) outright. Grounds below, both from this tree's own evidence.

(a) AND (b) ARE NOT ALTERNATIVES AND THE SWEEP'S FRAMING OF THEM AS ALTERNATIVES IS THE ONE THING I
WOULD CHANGE ABOUT THE BRIEF. (a) refuses a SPELLING. (b) refuses the CLASS. The measurement that
separates them is the one nobody had run, and I ran it.

=====================================================================================
THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDES IT: A FINITE VALUE DOES THE SAME DAMAGE AS inf
=====================================================================================
FAB_ALPHA driven through the fabric sweep's own harness (/tmp/fabsweep/cell.py, unmodified, real
tree, fresh subprocess per cell):

    FAB_ALPHA=1e20   aux=0.5155787467956543  composed=2.7893991470336914  nonfinite grads 0/23
    FAB_ALPHA=1e24   aux=0.5156660079956055  composed=2.765979766845703   nonfinite grads 0/23
    FAB_ALPHA=1e26   aux=0.5150710344314575  composed=2.943258285522461   nonfinite grads 15/23
    FAB_ALPHA=1e28   aux=nan                 composed=nan                 nonfinite grads 19/23
    FAB_ALPHA=1e30   aux=nan                 composed=nan                 nonfinite grads 19/23
    FAB_ALPHA=1e300  aux=nan                 composed=nan                 nonfinite grads 19/23
    FAB_ALPHA=-1e300 aux=nan                 composed=nan                 nonfinite grads 19/23
    FAB_ALPHA=nan    aux=nan                 composed=nan                 nonfinite grads 19/23   (the sweep's cell, reproduced)

1e28 is BIT-FOR-BIT the harm the sweep filed as [critical] FAB_ALPHA=nan, and it is a finite number
a type check and a finiteness check both admit. 1e26 IS WORSE THAN EITHER: the loss still reads
0.515 / 2.94 -- a perfectly ordinary pair of numbers a ledger would print without comment -- while
15 of 23 gradient-carrying tensors are ALREADY non-finite. That is a partially-poisoned population
reporting a healthy run, which is a strictly harder defect to see than a nan loss.

The same shape in OPT, through the opt sweep's own harness (/tmp/sw/cell.py, unmodified):

    OPT_LR=1e30 -> spine.assemble.build OK; OPT.build OK, AdamW constructed with `lr: 1e+30`;
                   OPT.lr_at over the 8-point grid returns [1e+28 ... 5e+28]; six maybe_step calls
                   all report (True, ..., False, False); OPT.counters reports opt.step: 6,
                   opt.backward: 6, no alarm anywhere -- and the harness's own parameter check
                   reads  "p_finite": false, "p_sample": "[nan, nan, nan]".

Every one of opt/api.py::build's eleven startup refusals passes 1e30, exactly as they pass inf.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RULING, STATED PLAINLY: a rule that refuses nan/inf and stops there closes the
four values the sweep happened to drive and leaves the mechanism open. That is not a hypothetical
risk -- IT IS THE EXACT FAILURE THIS RUN WAS CONVENED OVER. src/fabric/api.py::build already refuses
eleven magnitude levers at nan and +inf, and the comment immediately above that refusal enumerates
what it declined to cover: "Nor does this touch the levers whose negative side is a different
question -- FAB_ALPHA, FAB_ROUTE_T, FAB_HALT_MAX, FAB_BAL_FLOOR, FAB_SPAWN_FLOOR,
FAB_ROUTE_REGION_W, FAB_MUT, FAB_PRESSURE". Five of those six carry the identical critical defect
today. A refusal is only as good as the list its author thought of, and the author of the best one
in this tree left the list short by five. (a) alone repeats that pattern one level up.

=====================================================================================
WHAT (a) COSTS: MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED
=====================================================================================
I applied (a) to a full copy of the tree at /tmp/rule/tree -- ten lines in
src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce: OverflowError added to the except tuple, plus a finiteness check
raising LeverError with the generated env name and the raw string -- and ran the suite.

    test_ownership   base exit=0   patched exit=0   BYTE-IDENTICAL output
    test_census      base exit=0   patched exit=0   BYTE-IDENTICAL output
    test_assemble    base exit=0   patched exit=0   BYTE-IDENTICAL output
    test_couplings   base exit=0   patched exit=0   BYTE-IDENTICAL output
    test_derive      base exit=0   patched exit=0   BYTE-IDENTICAL output
    test_contract    base exit=0   patched exit=0   BYTE-IDENTICAL output
    test_fabric      base exit=0   patched exit=0   BYTE-IDENTICAL output

Seven of seven, byte for byte, against an unpatched copy of the same layout. And on the patched
tree the headline cell becomes:

    FAB_ALPHA=nan   -> stage=assemble  LeverError: FAB_ALPHA='nan' is not a finite number...
    FAB_ALPHA=inf   -> stage=assemble  LeverError: FAB_ALPHA='inf' is not a finite number...
    FAB_ALPHA=-inf  -> stage=assemble  LeverError: FAB_ALPHA='-inf' is not a finite number...
    FAB_ALPHA=1e999 -> stage=assemble  LeverError: FAB_ALPHA='1e999' is not a finite number...

THREE INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENTS SAY (a) TAKES NOTHING AWAY:
  1. ZERO of the 262 declared levers has a non-finite DEFAULT (/tmp/rule/t4.py, over every
     registered LeverSet).
  2. ZERO lever help strings declare a non-finite meaning. I scanned all 262 for
     inf/infinit/nan/unbounded/"no cap"/"no ceiling"/"no limit"; the six hits are the substring
     "inf" inside the word "InfoNCE" and "grow unbounded" in DOM.manage's prose. Nothing declares
     +inf as "no cap".
  3. ZERO of the 75 ACCEPTED_LEGITIMATE cells the six sweeps found is non-finite. All 75 are ZEROS
     (fabric 25, opt-lm-train 11, sig-tok 16, domains-memory 9, world-cap-ckpt 8, eval-data 6).
  4. ZERO configurations in the repository set any lever to a non-finite value: grepped every
     PREFIX_FIELD=nan|inf|-inf|1e{3+ digits} across the tree excluding .git/runs/.rework, and the
     only three hits are the prose of src/fabric/api.py's own comment about FAB_BALANCE=nan.

So (a)'s per-Lever opt-out has, today, no user. DECLARE IT ANYWAY -- it is the thing that makes the
rule falsifiable rather than absolute, and the day a lever wants +inf to mean "no cap" the opt-out
is the difference between one declaration and a revert.

=====================================================================================
WHY (b) IS THE ANSWER, AND WHAT IT REALLY COSTS
=====================================================================================
`choices=` IS THE PRECEDENT, AND THE MACHINERY GENERALISES FURTHER THAN THE BRIEF ASSUMED. I read
it and drove it. It is an optional kwarg on Lever.__init__; it is validated AT DECLARATION TIME
against the default ("default {default!r} is not among choices"); it is checked inside
Lever.coerce AFTER coercion; and it raises LeverError naming the generated env name and the value.
That is the exact shape a `domain=` needs, in the exact place, raising the exact idiom. It even
works on numeric levers today (MEASURED, /tmp/rule/t2.py):

    YY_G float, choices=(0.0,0.5,1.0):  '7' -> "LeverError: YY_G=7.0 must be one of [0.0, 0.5, 1.0]"
                                        'nan' -> "LeverError: YY_G=nan must be one of [...]"   (nan != nan)
                                        'inf' -> "LeverError: YY_G=inf must be one of [...]"

So `choices=` ALREADY refuses non-finite floats on the 0 levers that carry it -- it is precedent
AND working code. Its limit is that it ENUMERATES and cannot BOUND, which every affected file in
the tree already says in as many words.

THE PRICE OF (b), ITEMISED, BECAUSE IT IS NOT ZERO AND IT IS NOT THE 207 DECLARATIONS EITHER:
  - Lever.__slots__ +1, Lever.__init__ +1 kwarg, one declaration-time check (default must satisfy
    its own domain -- the mirror of the existing choices check), one check in coerce, and one field
    on LeverView. LeverView has exactly ONE producer (spine/lever.py:346, Config.lever) and NO
    consumer anywhere in src/, tests/ or tools/, so that field is free.
  - NO census row, NO new environment name, NO generated-document row: a domain is an attribute of
    a declaration that already exists, not a new knob. tests/test_census.py joins on lever NAMES
    and reads no other Lever field (grepped: no .default, no .unit, no .choices, no ._levers).
  - THE REAL COST IS PROSE, AND IT IS TEN CITATIONS. Ten places in seven files assert, as a
    load-bearing premise, that a Lever HAS no range facility -- and several use it to justify why a
    bound lives in a package body instead:
        src/spine/derive.py:371, src/spine/derive.py:673, src/opt/api.py:688,
        src/opt/levers.py:274, src/lm/api.py:205, src/lm/api.py:235,
        src/capacity/api.py:661, src/capacity/api.py:677, src/sig/api.py:806,
        src/train/levers.py:187
    Two of those are inside RAISED ERROR MESSAGES an operator sees (spine/derive.py:371 and :673).
    O13 will not catch these -- it checks that a cited path::symbol exists, not that a sentence
    about it is still true -- so this is a hand sweep of seven files and it must be budgeted.
    It is also, in my reading, a reason to do (b) rather than a reason not to: ten independent
    authors each wrote "the spine cannot express this, so I am doing it here", which is the tree
    telling you where the facility should have been.

  - THE HAZARD (b) CARRIES, AND FAB NAMED IT BEFORE I DID: "a guard invented for a value nobody has
    shown to be wrong is the untrippable-guard class one level up" (src/fabric/api.py::build). I
    tested my own enthusiasm against it and it survived only partly. MEASURED: FAB_ALPHA=-1.0,
    FAB_CENT_EMA=2.0, FAB_CENT_EMA=100.0 and FAB_HALT_MAX=1000.0 all run CLEAN on two passes --
    aux 0.512/0.521/0.512/0.512, composed ~3.007, 0/23 non-finite. A `domain=(0.0, 1.0)` on
    cent_ema would refuse a value this tree has not shown to be wrong. THAT IS WHY (b) IS
    INCREMENTAL AND EVIDENCE-LED IN R2: populate `domain=` only where a measurement exists, and
    leave it absent everywhere else, where R1's floor still stands.

=====================================================================================
WHY (c) LOSES
=====================================================================================
Not on taste, on this tree's record. FAB wrote the per-package refusal, at the right entry point,
in the right idiom, with an argued comment -- and it is the ONLY package that did, and it missed
five of its own levers by name in a list it wrote itself. CAP wrote one too: new_valve's twenty-one
line negative-lift refusal is `float(cap.lift) < 0`, false for nan and for +inf, so CAP_LIFT=nan
walks past it. SIG wrote one: `if temp <= 0.0`, three lines above the division, false for NaN. OPT
wrote eleven: every one an order comparison, and NaN is ordered against nothing. The opt sweep
found the structural tell and it is the strongest single sentence in the six reports: every guard
that HELD against NaN has the inverted-chain form (`if not 0.0 <= x < 1.0`), and the three levers
that are safe today are safe BY GRAMMAR, NOT BY INTENT. 207 per-package refusals is not thirteen
authors implementing one policy; it is thirteen authors each rediscovering that `x < 0` is false
for NaN, at thirteen different times, some of them not yet.

=====================================================================================
WHY (d) LOSES, AND WHAT IT COSTS WHEN THE NEXT LEVER IS ADDED
=====================================================================================
(d)'s premise is that an operator typing `nan` gets what they asked for. Two measurements refute it.
  1. THE OPERATOR DOES NOT HAVE TO TYPE nan. `1e999` parses to inf (MEASURED: float lever -> inf,
     int lever -> the bare OverflowError). A number that looks like a big number is an infinity.
  2. WHAT THEY GET IS NOT THEIR VALUE, IT IS A FALSE REPORT. This tree's DID IT FIRE contract has
     three states, and NaN manufactures a fourth that renders as the second: a comparison that is
     false for EVERY possible value printing "armed, did not fire". Reproduced on the real tree at
     FAB_ALPHA=nan: aux nan, composed nan, 19/23 gradients non-finite, pop.cent permanently
     poisoned -- beside "Gate fab.halt: FIRED (mean halted mass nan vs halt_max=0.9)" and thirteen
     other gates reporting confidently over the poison. An operator asking for nan is not asking
     for the instrument to lie about it.
COST WHEN THE NEXT LEVER IS ADDED: every new float lever ships with this hole, silently, and
nothing in the declaration, the review or the suite tells its author. That is the cost the FAB
repair already paid once -- the defect did not close, it RELOCATED into the six levers the repair
named as out of scope, and it took a new instrument to find it there.

=====================================================================================
DOES ZERO BELONG IN THE RULING? NO -- AND HERE IS WHAT PROTECTS THE ZEROS THAT ARE DEFECTS
=====================================================================================
NO CENTRAL RULE MAY TOUCH 0. 75 of the sweeps' 828 cells are ACCEPTED_LEGITIMATE and every single
one is a zero: "0 means never freeze" (TOK_FREEZE_AT), "one wavelength spans the whole run"
(OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH), "start at the hard ceiling" (CAP_FAB_START, CAP_VOCAB_START), "the full
stack" (MEM_KEY_DEPTH -- also the shipped default), "0 derives it from the area count"
(DATA_PHASE_LIVE), "no curriculum" (FAB_DEPTH0), the declared DISARM (MEM_REKEY_EVERY), and the
eight FAB magnitude levers whose own build() says "Set the lever to 0.0 to switch the mechanism
off". A central 0 refusal breaks all 75 and refuses the SHIPPED DEFAULT in at least three places.

BUT ELEVEN OF THE THIRTY-FIVE HARMFUL FINDINGS ARE ZEROS, AND THEY ARE NOT A SEPARATE PROBLEM --
THEY ARE (b). Look at what they have in common: FAB_RANK, FAB_DK, FAB_EMB_HID, FAB_SLOTS,
FAB_HOPS, SIG_D, SIG_CONTRASTIVE_BATCH, TOK_MAX_BYTES, MEM_QUOTA, MEM_OWNERS are WIDTHS AND COUNTS
-- 0 means a tensor with no dimension, a vocabulary that cannot grow, a store with no rows -- and
FAB_MANAGE_EVERY is a CADENCE. Not one is a magnitude with an "off" reading. `domain=(1, None)` on
a width says exactly that, in the declaration, checkable, once. Under (a) alone these eleven need
eleven hand-written per-package refusals in five packages, which is (c) arriving through the back
door. THIS IS THE SECOND REASON (b) IS THE ANSWER AND (a) IS ONLY THE FLOOR: the zeros and the
infinities are one ruling under (b) and two unrelated work items under (a).
ONE ZERO IS NOT (b)'s AND MUST BE SAID: FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=0 also needs
src/spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows to refuse `< 1` where it today refuses only `< 0` -- the
function's own floor turns 0 into Flushes(1), the tightest cadence in the system, which is the
identical arithmetic it was repaired for at negatives on 2026-09-05.

=====================================================================================
THE REFUSAL IDIOM
=====================================================================================
Matches, exactly and without a new idiom. The established form is `raise spine.lever.LeverError`
naming the lever and the value at the FIRST read before anything is derived. Lever.coerce IS the
first read -- it is the function the tree's own O1 makes the only place an environment string
becomes a value -- and it already raises LeverError naming `env_name_for(prefix)` and the raw
string, twice, for the type failure and for choices. R1 and R2 both add a third clause to a
function that already has two of exactly this shape. Nothing new is introduced and nothing moves.
ONE PLACE WHERE I WOULD DEPART FROM THE IDIOM AND SAY SO: the message should print the RAW STRING
the operator typed (`FAB_ALPHA='1e999'`), not the coerced value (`FAB_ALPHA=inf`), because the two
differ here and the raw string is the thing the operator can search their shell history for.

=====================================================================================
D17: DOES THE SAME SWITCH RULE APPLY? ONE SWITCH, AND ONLY FOR (a)
=====================================================================================
The tree has ALREADY RULED on this generalisation and it ruled against it. src/ckpt/api.py's
REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD block says, in its own words: "It is NOT a precedent that a range refusal
gets a switch, and the tree it lands in is emphatic about that: lm/api.py::resolve,
opt/api.py::build and capacity/api.py::new_valve all refuse out-of-range lever values with no
switch of any kind... This switch exists because the owner asked for THIS refusal to be
turn-off-able, by name, in the same breath as ordering it -- and it is the only one in the tree
that was asked for." I take that at face value: D17 does not reach here on its own terms.

I NONETHELESS RECOMMEND ONE SWITCH FOR R1 AND NOT FOR R2, on a ground D17 does not supply. D17's
switch is about a POLICY the owner might reverse. R1's switch is about BLAST RADIUS: it is the only
change in this tree's history that alters the meaning of 207 declarations in one commit, and if my
four measurements have missed a legitimate non-finite configuration, the operator who finds it is
holding a shell and cannot proceed. R2 needs no switch because a `domain=` is per-declaration and
its blast radius is one lever; deleting the kwarg is already the switch.

THE SHAPE, AND IT IS CHEAPER THAN D17's BY FOUR SPELLINGS: `REFUSE_NON_FINITE = True` as a module
constant in src/spine/lever.py. ONE spelling, not five. The five REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD constants
are spelled five times only because O10 forbids the four sibling packages to import ckpt; spine
.lever is in O10's allowlist ("a package may import spine.{lever, units, derive, rng, wire}"), so
one constant in the file that owns parsing is reachable from everywhere by construction. Same
costs as D17's, stated the same way: turning it off is a code edit and not an environment
variable, there is no SPINE_REFUSE_NON_FINITE, it takes no census row, and an operator holding only
a shell cannot reach it. The one gain over D17's shape is that "does the refusal have a bad effect"
can be answered by flipping one name in one file rather than five in five.

WIRE_BUDGET: THIS COSTS ZERO EDGES, AND I CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. Neither R0, R1 nor R2
crosses a package boundary. A domain is an attribute of a declaration the owning package already
holds; the check runs inside spine.lever, which every package already imports; and no package needs
to read another's value to perform it. Six of twenty-five edges remain and this recommendation
spends none of them.

=====================================================================================
IF THE OWNER WILL FUND ONLY ONE THING
=====================================================================================
R0. It is one token, it converts ~220 cells tree-wide from an anonymous traceback to the tree's own
named refusal, and it decides nothing. R1 second: ten lines, seven test files byte-identical, 24 of
the 35 harmful findings closed. R2 is the one that actually ends the class, and it is also the one
that should not be rushed, because populating a domain without a measurement is the untrippable
guard FAB warned about.

=====================================================================================
THE MEASUREMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE IT (D11 requirement)
=====================================================================================
1. THE ONE I WOULD RUN FIRST, AND IT IS THE SAME HARNESS AT NEW VALUES. Re-drive all 97 float
   levers at {1e26, 1e30, -1e30} and all 110 int levers at {1e15, -1e15} through the existing
   per-package cells -- ~500 cells, one afternoon, the harnesses are still on disk at
   /tmp/fabsweep/, /tmp/sw/, /tmp/sigtok_sweep_5862/ and the domains-memory scratch. I ran 8 of
   those cells and 8 of 8 reproduced the inf harm exactly. IF THAT RATE HOLDS ACROSS THE 97, (a) is
   proved to be a spelling fix and (b) becomes mandatory rather than recommended. IF IT DOES NOT --
   if the large-finite harm is confined to a handful of residual/rate levers -- then (a) plus a
   domain on those few is the whole job and R2 shrinks to a dozen declarations.
2. THE FALSIFIER FOR (a), STILL OPEN BY CONSTRUCTION: a lever for which a non-finite value is the
   natural spelling of a legitimate configuration. I looked for it four ways (defaults, help text,
   the 75 declared specials, every configuration in the repository) and found none, which is why I
   recommend (a) -- but "none exists today" is not "none can exist", and it is exactly why the
   per-Lever opt-out ships with the rule rather than after it.
3. THE FALSIFIER FOR (b), AND IT IS THE ONE THAT WOULD MAKE ME WITHDRAW R2: take the twenty levers
   on the work list below, write a domain for each, and count how many have a bound this tree can
   DEFEND FROM A MEASUREMENT rather than from taste. If it is 20 of 20, (b) generalises and the
   remaining 187 follow as evidence arrives. If it is 6 of 20, then (b) delivers a facility that
   187 levers carry as `domain=None`, the honest answer is (a) plus per-package refusals for the
   eleven geometry zeros, and I would say so.
4. AND THE CHEAP ONE THAT SHOULD RUN REGARDLESS: apply R1 to a branch and run
   tests/test_determinism.py plus one real short training run. I ran the seven static/behavioural
   suites and got byte-identical output; I did NOT run a training loop, and the composition root
   halts at CAP.startup_refusals today so I could not have run one end to end.

legitimate_specials:
THE DENOMINATOR, AND IT IS THE MOST DECISION-RELEVANT NUMBER IN THIS REPORT: 75 of the six sweeps'
828 cells are ACCEPTED_LEGITIMATE, and EVERY ONE OF THEM IS A ZERO. Fabric 25, sig-tok 16
(15 zeros + SIG_TEMP's high arm), opt-lm-train 11, domains-memory 9, world-cap-ckpt 8, eval-data 6.
NOT ONE IS nan, +inf OR -inf.

I checked that four independent ways rather than taking the six reports' word for it:
  (1) NON-FINITE DEFAULTS over all 262 declared levers in all 13 registered LeverSets: ZERO.
      Measured, /tmp/rule/t4.py.
  (2) HELP TEXT declaring a non-finite meaning: ZERO. Scanned all 262 help strings for
      inf / infinit / nan / unbounded / "no cap" / "no ceiling" / "no limit". Six hits, all
      spurious: five are the substring "inf" inside "InfoNCE" (SIG.contrastive_batch,
      SIG.positive_radius_windows, SIG.prototype_frac, SIG.floor_kinds) and one is DOM.manage's
      "lets it grow unbounded", which describes the mechanism and not a value.
  (3) CONFIGURATIONS IN THE REPOSITORY setting a lever non-finite: ZERO. Grepped every
      PREFIX_FIELD=nan|inf|-inf|1e{3+ digits} across the tree excluding .git, runs/ and .rework/;
      the only three hits are inside src/fabric/api.py's own comment ABOUT FAB_BALANCE=nan.
  (4) THE SUITE under the rule: seven test files, byte-identical output patched vs unpatched.

CONCLUSION FOR THE CENTRAL-VS-PER-PACKAGE QUESTION: a finiteness refusal in
src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce would wrongly refuse ZERO of the 75, and the three cells the
fabric report flagged as "provably identical to an already-legal zero"
(FAB_ROUTE_T=nan/-inf, FAB_SPAWN_MULT=-inf, FAB_SPAWN_FLOOR=-inf) lose nothing an operator can
still ask for by typing 0. A rule refusing ZERO would break all 75 and would refuse the SHIPPED
DEFAULT in at least three places (MEM_KEY_DEPTH=0 "the full stack", OPT_GRAD_CLIP=0.0 "OFF, which
is what every recorded number in this project was measured under", FAB_HOP_SUP=0.0 and the other
FAB magnitude levers whose build() prints "Set the lever to 0.0 to switch the mechanism off").

THE ONE LEGITIMATE SPECIAL THE RULING PHASE MUST NOT LOSE, carried forward from the domains-memory
report because it is the only case where refusing a value would destroy a DECLARED meaning:
MEM_REKEY_EVERY=0 is the declared DISARM for ONE of its two readers (memory/api.py::maintain) while
rekey_period returns Windows(0) into RUN.Cadences.due, which by its own contract fires every window
at period 0. Two mechanisms, one number, opposite answers. That is a real defect and it is NOT a
finiteness question -- it belongs to whatever ruling settles cadence-zero alongside
FAB_MANAGE_EVERY=0 and DOM_MANAGE_EVERY=0. Do not fold it into this one.
